posts.name: AI Scaling
posts.cooked:
AI Scaling is hiring five full-time AI Implementation Consultants and Partner Coaches.

This is primarily a one-on-one coaching role for agency owners, but it requires real implementation experience. You will teach new partners how their agency systems work and occasionally help configure workspaces, CRM pipelines, automated workflows, AI agents, and client solutions.

What you will do

  • Coach assigned agency owners through a structured three-month ramp
  • Teach nontechnical partners how to use AI Scaling’s platform and agent copilots
  • Explain CRM pipelines, workflows, automation, AI agents, and B2B sales processes
  • Provide asynchronous support through Slack
  • Help troubleshoot or configure partner and client workspaces when needed
  • Track partner competency, time to first sale, and client satisfaction

What we are looking for

  • At least two years of hands-on experience implementing CRM, automation, or AI systems
  • Experience as a freelancer, agency owner, agency operator, or implementation specialist
  • Working knowledge of tools such as n8n, Make, Zapier, GoHighLevel, HubSpot, Airtable, Notion, or Monday.com
  • Experience building automated workflows or AI agents
  • Strong understanding of B2B sales and the ability to explain processes clearly
  • Clear, professional spoken and written English
  • Comfortable teaching clients on camera and working independently
  • Course creation, SOP writing, or educational content experience is a plus
  • Cold email marketing experience is helpful but not required

Role details

  • Full-time, Monday through Friday
  • Remote and open worldwide
  • Flexible eight-hour shift within our operating window
  • Starting compensation: $6,000 per month
  • Performance bonus: up to 20%
  • Reports directly to the COO
  • Hiring five people and starting as soon as possible

Apply here:

AI Scaling

AI Implementation Consultant and Partner Coach | AI Scaling Careers

Apply for a full-time remote role coaching AI Scaling licensee partners on AI implementation, CRM systems, automation, sales, and agency operations.

Please apply through the link rather than sending a forum direct message. The application includes a short video so we can evaluate technical communication and teaching ability.

posts.name: Jamal Cherki BOUMSIK
posts.cooked:
Interested — I am applying through your careers page as well; posting here so you have the substance in front of you.

Two things that may be relevant to how you screen for this role.

First, I have done the implementation side, not just studied it. I run an AI sales agent on WhatsApp in production for a real-estate agency — it takes Meta ad leads, qualifies them, sends documents and pricing from a database rather than from the model, books appointments, and hands off to a human when it leaves its scope. I also built the operating system of a construction company on Airtable and n8n, tying quotes to site interventions, invoicing and cash position. Both are live systems with real users, which means I have had to explain them to non-technical owners who needed to run them without me.

Second, the part of coaching that usually decides whether a partner reaches first sale is not tool training. It is teaching them what not to automate yet. Before this work I spent fifteen years in industrial operations and procurement, and the most common failure I see is an agency owner automating a process nobody has agreed on. A quote that goes out without a human check is not a productivity gain, it is exposure. That distinction is teachable, and it is what shortens time to first sale.

One question so I can be useful rather than generic: for the three-month ramp, is the bottleneck you are seeing today on the partner’s technical confidence, or on their B2B sales motion? I would prepare differently for each.

For transparency: I work from Casablanca, fully remote, same hours as Western Europe, and I coach in English, French or Arabic. English is my working language in writing and on calls, though it is not my mother tongue — I would rather say that now than have you discover it in a screening call.
